answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network ties node registration to cryptographic stake burning calibrated by a superlinear cost curve: burning cost scales quadratically, C(k) = b * k^2, for k concurrent identities. Anchoring digital identity minting to verifiable physical computation—such as proving quartz crystal frequency stability under heavy ferrous metal shielding at each wharf docking validator—forces real economic friction, rendering multi-identity spoofing mathematically cost-prohibitive.
